name: The solar system, stars and orbits

terms.definition: One star (the Sun), eight planets, dwarf planets and natural satellites (moons); part of the Milky Way galaxy.
A cloud of dust and gas (nebula) pulled together by gravity, which heats up until fusion starts.
A star in a stable state: the outward pressure from fusion energy balances the inward force of gravity.

terms.term: Life cycle of a Sun-sized star
terms.definition: Main sequence → red giant → white dwarf → black dwarf.
terms.examiner: Separate Physics. Much larger stars become red super giants, supernovae, then neutron stars or black holes.

terms.definition: Produces all the naturally occurring elements; heavier ones than iron form in supernovae, which spread them through the universe.
Gravity provides the force that keeps a planet or satellite in orbit; its speed is constant but its velocity changes.
terms.examiner: Separate Physics, higher tier. A change in speed changes the radius of orbit.
